recentItems.title: Bodies of victims in Nepal's flash floods arrive in Nuwakot
recentItems.description:
(30 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot, Nepal - 30 August 2026
++PART MUTE++
1. Various of rescue personnel taking away body bags from helicopter
2. Helicopter lands
3. Various of rescued persons walking away after being brought by helicopter
4. Various of essentials being unloaded from a helicopter
5. Helicopter lands
6. Various of essential goods being loaded onto a helicopter to be taken to flood affected areas
7. Helicopter takes off carrying essentials to flood affected areas
8. Another helicopter flies away
9. Aerial shot of overflowing Trishuli river ++MUTE++
10. Various of drone of damaged buildings and overflowing Trishuli river ++MUTE++
STORYLINE:
Rescue and recovery teams in Nuwakot on Sunday were receiving bodies of victims in Nepal's devastating flash floods.

The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 750 dead and over 3,000 people missing after the latest updates on Sunday. 

Nepal’s disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 734 with 2,498 people missing, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, including over a hundred Nepalis and people from over a dozen countries.

AP Video shot by Rishi Lekhi and Rajesh Kumar Singh

recentItems.title: Nepal issues warning after reports of renewed flooding
recentItems.description:
(30 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot, Nepal - 30 August 2026
1. Various of swollen Trishuli river after fresh water surge warning in morning 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Dhading, Nepal - 30 August 2026 
2. Various of residents standing on higher ground watching flooding
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Victoria Milko, Associated Press 
“We're in Dhading, where we're seeing some of the roads are opening up, including parts of the main Nepal Highway that was shut down. The highway serves as a major way for things to get in and out of Kathmandu, and there's fears there may be shortages ahead of the autumn festival season. Behind us, you're seeing along the river. We've been getting warnings all morning that the river levels might be rising, and that water is moving very, very fast. So locals have been advised to move way to higher zones, away to safety. You can see also the extent of the destruction. There's entire homes, there's tractors, farming equipment, vehicles completely submerged in the sediment by the riverside. I think the extent of the damage is still being surveyed because areas are very hard to access.”  
4. Various of damaged bridge
5. Various of structures underneath mud
STORYLINE:
Nepal's disaster authority and the Flood Forecasting Division issued early-morning alerts to residents of Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts on Sunday, advising them to stay vigilant amid reports of renewed flooding in the Bhotekoshi.

The warning came after Chinese authorities shared information indicating increased water flow upstream.

The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 691 dead and over 3,000 people missing after China’s latest update on Sunday. 

Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, while Nepal’s disaster agency said late Saturday that the death toll had climbed to 675 with 2,498 people missing.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

AP Video by Rajesh Kumar Singh and Shonal Ganguly

recentItems.title: Tea, a beloved social beverage, is a way of life in Turkey
recentItems.description:
(30 Aug 2026) 
TURKEY TEA

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

LENGTH: 4:50

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Istanbul, Turkey -  26 August 2026
1. Various of tea being served in a teahouse to men playing cards around a table 
2. Person drinking tea during game
3. Tea glass amid background of teahouse
4. Traditional kettles 
5. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Salim Varici, 42, tea shop owner: 
"Tea is a culture. Tea is one of our national beverages. The conversation that goes with tea is something else entirely. How many glasses of water, energy drinks or Ayran (a yoghurt drink) can you actually drink? Maybe one or two. If you're really sick, maybe three. But with tea... I know of a person, right here in this establishment, who drank 52 glasses. A person sat at a table and (said) 'give me tea, give me tea, give me tea' and drank 52 glasses. Tea is different _ the way you drink it, the conversation that accompanies it. You might sit and chat for five hours; you can drink tea intermittently throughout those five hours, there’s no problem with that."

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Istanbul, Turkey - 27 August 2026
6. Mid of two women sitting outside a shop, drinking tea
7. Close of tea glasses
8. Women talking, drinking tea

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Istanbul, Turkey -  26 August 2026
9. Mid of two women drinking tea inside restaurant 
10. Mid of a thermos with tea, a thin-waisted tea glass nearby, Bosporus and bridge in the background
11. Close of Huseyin Cicekdal drinking tea 
12. Close of tea glass 
13. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Huseyin Cicekdal, 57, tea lover: 
"It’s cold where I come from. Tea is very valuable for us. Whether it’s in the village or here, too. There’s a lot of tea consumption where I’m from. When you went to visit someone (in the old days), there wasn’t coffee. Coffee has become more common lately. In fact, there didn’t used to be coffee, you couldn’t find it in every home. But tea, if you go somewhere to sit, they immediately say, ‘put on some tea'."

14. Mid of men at a teahouse being served tea
15. Close of table, and tea glass being set down in saucer
16. Close of tea glasses in a dishwasher rack
17. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Ramazan Guvenc, 43, tea shop manager: 
"People who are tea addicts drink tea in a thin-waisted glass. The reason is this: if you drink too much, it gives you nausea. So, because it is drunk hot, because it is a hot product, a thin-waisted glass is preferred so that it doesn’t cool down. Also, with the thin-waisted glass, because the mouth of the glass is narrow, it is more pleasant to drink from."

18. Various of two men talking and drinking tea
19. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Ramazan Guvenc, 43, tea shop manager: 
"We brew the tea according to my own recommendation. We fill the (kettle with) water, and after filling the water, we add hot water on top (in the teapot.) Then we put the tea leaves on top and lightly moisten them, and place it (the teapot) over the steam. When you place it over the steam, it brews by itself. Once it has brewed on its own, it releases its flavor and it shouldn’t be stirred. When you stir it, the tea dust gets mixed in, so the aroma is lost, it loses its meaning, and the tea becomes cloudy."

20. Various of tea being brewed
21. Teapots sitting on top of traditional tea urn 
22. SOUNDBITE (Turkish) Dursun Kara, 69, tea lover: 
"Since I’m alone at home, there’s no one to chat with. But when you come here, you can have a good time with friends, joke around, laugh and have a bit of fun."

23. Close of tea being stirred in tea glass
24. Kara outside the teahouse with friends, drinking tea
25. Close of tea glass and silver spoon

recentItems.title: Taiwan's oldest panda celebrates 22nd birthday
recentItems.description:
(30 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Taipei Zoo, Taipei City, Taiwan - 30 August 2026
1. Various of panda Yuanyuan walking into her enclosure and starting to eat her birthday ice cake that features her 22nd birthday
2. SOUNDBITE (Mandarin) Kao Shih-cheng, 38, Ramen shop employee:
“She (Panda Yuanyuan) is 22 years old this year. She is already old for a panda. This is equivalent to a human being between 60 and 70 years old. A panda can live up to 30 years. Currently, the oldest living panda is in Mexico. Its name is Xin Xin. It is 35 years old this year. For a human, it’s over a hundred years old.” 
3. Various of panda Yuanyuan eating fruits from her birthday ice cake 
4. Various of zoo visitors looking at panda Yuanyuan 
5. Zoom out panda Yuanyuan pushing her ice cake, visitors shouting in astonishment 
6. Mid of panda Yuanyuan hiding behind her ice cake 
7. Various of zoo staffers assembling Panda Yuanyuan’s ice cake before the panda enters her enclosure 
8. Various of panda Yuanyuan’s ice cake before she enters her enclosure 
STORYLINE:
The oldest panda living in Taiwan, Yuanyuan, celebrated her 22nd birthday Sunday morning with dozens of her fans wishing her happy birthday in front of her air-conditioned enclosure. 

Yuanyuan was the first female panda in the world to give birth to cubs in Taiwan. 

Yuanyuan’s birthday ice cake was made with fruits and vegetables, and was frozen to make it into the shape of a train. 

Kao Shih-cheng, a 38-year-old ramen shop employee and avid panda fan, said, “She (Panda Yuanyuan) is 22 years old this year. She is already old for a panda. This is equivalent to a human being between 60 and 70 years old."

Female panda Yuanyuan arrived in Taiwan in December 2008 along with male panda Tuantuan as a gift to Taiwan from China. Tuantuan died in November 2022.

AP Video by Taijing Wu

recentItems.title: Helicopter transports those rescued or evacuated due to Nepal flash floods
recentItems.description:
(30 Aug 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Nuwakot District, Nepal - 30 August 2026
1. Various of helipad, choppers bringing in goods and rescued people
STORYLINE:
As rescue efforts continued in communities buried by catastrophic flash floods along the Nepal - China border, authorities were still finding survivors and transporting them to safety.

At relief centers, families of missing people waited anxiously for news of their loved ones as the death toll and the number of people unaccounted for continued to rise.

The combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 691 dead and over 3,000 people missing after China’s latest update on Sunday. Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, while Nepal’s disaster agency said late Saturday that the death toll had climbed to 675 with 2,498 people missing.

More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal so far.

In Nuwakot, one of the Nepali districts devastated by the floods, helicopters arrived loaded with boxes and bags of aid, including clothes, instant noodles, crackers and rice. Others returned from the flood-hit areas carrying survivors.

recentItems.title: The male midwives battling against pregnancy deaths
recentItems.description:
(30 Aug 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mohale's Hoek, Lesotho - 10 July 2026

1. Various of male midwife Ntlhane Sehloho examining a pregnant woman and listening to the foetal heartbeat at Mpharane Health Centre 
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Ntlhane Sehloho, male midwife:
"So, as I was growing, our village is far away from the health facility, so most women who are pregnant, some were delivering at home, so it was just a mess. We were still young, we were not supposed to see that, some were dying and all that, so I said why are these women delivering at home? I didn’t understand that they had to travel over long distance. There was no transport or anything. So, I then said that I’m going to grow and I’m going to be a nurse.”

3. Mid of Sehloho talking to pregnant woman during an antenatal consultation 
4. Close of Sehloho measuring the woman's abdomen 
5. Mid of Sehloho checking the woman's pulse and listening for the baby's heartbeat 
6. SOUNDBITE (English) Ntlhane Sehloho, male midwife:
"There are quite a lot, and if you can go around the country, in most of our health centres, the ones in charge are those male midwives and even in a class, you will find that we have twenty student nurses or student midwives and ten males. So that says for Lesotho it’s normal to be a midwife.”      

7. Mid of Sehloho taking medical records from women before an antenatal consultation
8. Close-up of medical records on the table 
9. Various of Sehloho picking up records and writing in them
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Ntlhane Sehloho, male midwife:
"I’m approaching a century now (he means decade) serving this nation and I’m so proud. When I look back and say, this child? I know I was the one delivering them. When I see those twins that I met at the maternity hospital? I know they are my child. I’m so happy, I’m looking back with a happy smile."

11. Wide of mountainous landscape outside Mpharane Health Centre in Mohale’s Hoek, Lesotho

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Mohale's Hoek, Lesotho - 9 July 2026 

12. Wide of community members gathered at UN family planning event for information about services on maternal and family health
13. Wide of people speaking to a UN family planning representative 
14. SOUNDBITE (English) Blandina Motaung, Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights Coordinator for UNFPA:
"For a midwife to achieve positive outcome of the pregnancy, she or he has to go to walk with this pregnant woman throughout the path of pregnancy until delivery. Therefore, for men, it becomes an issue of providing that psychosocial support more than it is provided by the female midwives."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mohale's Hoek, Lesotho - 10 July 2026

15. Mid of Sehloho talking to pregnant woman during an antenatal consultation at Mpharane Health Centre
16. Mid of Sehloho examining the abdomen of a pregnant woman 

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mohale's Hoek, Lesotho - 9 July 2026 

17. SOUNDBITE (English) Blandina Motaung, Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights Coordinator for UNFPA:
"For female midwives, the majority of them would have gone or will go through the process of pregnancy and childbirth, but for the men, because they have not gone through the process, they become more vigilant and more attentive to the nitty gritty, and that is its own improved quality of care that they provide."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mohale's Hoek, Lesotho - 10 July 2026

18. Various of Mpolokeng Mafereka arriving at Mpharane Health Centre for antenatal care
19. Mid of signage outside the consultation and delivery room 
20. Wide of Mafereka preparing to be examined by Ntlhane 
22. SOUNDBITE (Sesotho) Mpolokeng Mafereka, expectant mother:
